post.summary: Authenticates a user and returns access credentials (JWT access token and refresh token).
post.description:
This is a public endpoint that does not require authentication.
The access token is a JWT that should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent authenticated requests.
The refresh token can be used to obtain a new access token when the current one expires.
Failed login attempts may be logged for security monitoring.

requestBody.description: The login request containing user credentials (email and password).

200.description: Login successful or validation error occurred.

post.summary: Refreshes the access token using a valid refresh token and returns a new access token.
post.description:
This is a public endpoint that does not require an active Access Token.
It is used to obtain new credentials when the current Access Token has expired.
The system validates the provided refresh token against the user's stored records.
On success, a new Access Token and a new Refresh Token are issued (Rotation).

requestBody.description: The request containing the refresh token to be validated and exchanged for a new access token.

200.description: Token refreshed successfully.

post.summary: Changes the password for the currently authenticated user.
post.description:
This endpoint requires authentication. The user must provide a valid JWT Bearer token in the Authorization header.
The current password must be provided to verify the user's identity before changing to the new password.
The new password must meet the system's password complexity requirements.
Upon successful password change, new tokens are issued and the user should update their stored credentials.

requestBody.description: The request containing the current password and the new password to set.

200.description: Password changed successfully or validation error occurred.

post.summary: Activates a user account using an activation token sent via email.
post.description:
This is a public endpoint that does not require authentication.
Activation tokens are typically sent via email after user registration.
Tokens are single-use and have an expiration time for security.
Once activated, the user can log in with their credentials.

requestBody.description: The request containing the activation token and user identifier.

200.description: Activation successful or validation error occurred.
OK

post.summary: Initiates the password reset process by sending a reset email to the user's registered email address.
post.description:
This is a public endpoint that does not require authentication.
For security reasons, this endpoint always returns OK (Status 200) regardless of whether the email exists in the system.
If the email exists, a password reset email with a time-limited token will be sent.
If the email doesn't exist, no action is taken but the response is identical.
This behavior prevents email enumeration attacks.

requestBody.description: The request containing the email address of the user requesting password reset.

200.description: Password reset request processed successfully.

post.summary: Resets the user's password using a valid password reset token received via email.
post.description:
This is a public endpoint that does not require authentication.
The reset token is obtained from the password reset email sent via the forgot-password endpoint.
Reset tokens are single-use and have a limited validity period for security.
The new password must meet the system's password complexity requirements.
After successful password reset, the user can log in with their new password.

requestBody.description: The request containing the reset token and the new password.

200.description: Password reset successfully or validation error occurred.

post.summary: Logs out the currently authenticated user by invalidating their refresh tokens.
post.description:
This endpoint requires authentication. The user must provide a valid JWT Bearer token in the Authorization header.
Logging out invalidates all refresh tokens associated with the user's current session.
The access token will remain valid until its natural expiration, but cannot be refreshed after logout.
For complete security, clients should also discard the access token locally after logout.

200.description: Logout successful.

post.summary: Revokes all refresh tokens for a specific user by their unique identifier.
post.description:
This endpoint requires authentication and the string Users.ManageTokens permission.
This is an administrative action that forcefully logs out a user by invalidating all their refresh tokens.
The target user's existing access tokens will remain valid until their natural expiration.
This is useful for security purposes, such as when a user's account is compromised or when enforcing policy changes.
The user will need to log in again to obtain new tokens.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier (GUID) of the user whose tokens should be revoked.

200.description: Tokens revoked successfully or validation error occurred.

get.summary: Retrieves all users from the system with filtering and pagination support.
get.description:
This endpoint requires the string Users.Read permission.
The Page property in filterParameters is automatically adjusted to 1 if a value less than 1 is provided.
The PageSize property in filterParameters is automatically capped at 100 if a larger value is provided.
The filter parameters allow for advanced searching and sorting capabilities.
Returns user information including email, name, roles, and permissions.

200.description: Returns the paginated list of users successfully.

post.summary: Registers a new user in the system through self-registration.
post.description:
This is a public endpoint that allows users to self-register without authentication.
The user will be created with default permissions and no roles assigned.
Password must meet the system's security requirements.
Email addresses must be unique in the system.
The second parameter (false) indicates this is not an admin registration.

requestBody.description: The registration request containing user details (email, password, first name, last name, etc.).

200.description: User registered successfully or validation error occurred.

post.summary: Registers a new user in the system by an administrator with pre-assigned roles and permissions.
post.description:
This endpoint requires the string Users.Create permission.
Unlike self-registration, admin-created users may have pre-assigned roles and permissions.
The admin can specify initial roles and permissions during user creation.
Email addresses must be unique in the system.
This is useful for creating user accounts with specific access levels from the start.

requestBody.description: The registration request containing user details including roles and permissions to be assigned by the admin.

200.description: User registered successfully or validation error occurred.

delete.summary: Deletes a user from the system.

put.summary: Activates or deactivates a user account.
put.description:
This endpoint requires the string Users.Update permission.
Activating a user sets their Active status to true and confirms their email.
Deactivating a user sets their Active status to false, preventing login.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The unique identifier (GUID) of the user to activate or deactivate.

parameters.name: activate
parameters.description: Whether to activate (true) or deactivate (false) the user account.

200.description: User status updated successfully or validation error.

This endpoint requires authentication. Users can only update their own profile.
Only the first name and last name fields can be updated through this endpoint.
